clue.text: Stopped copper meeting informer in Belfast

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
in Northern Irish slang a tout is a police informer

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish policeman sits down with his informant in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer meeting a grass, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol CU. TOUT is the Northern Irish word for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that has stopped running suddenly is said to have died or failed, the phrasal-verb sense here.

clue.text: Shut up about waste

parts.note: C, short for circa, is Latin for about
to lose an opportunity is to waste it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet on the subject of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up a shop or house is to lock it, a direct synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: End up with performer on strike

parts.note: a turn is a performer doing an act in a variety show
workers who are out have walked off the job

explanation.surface: A performer ends up joining a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to prove eventually to be so, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Raised immediately about article on diamonds in varying states

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first pair of pieces surrounds the article and suit

parts.note: something raised is lifted high
money paid down is paid at once, on the spot
an is the indefinite article
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player hurriedly picks up a diamond in a run of fluctuating fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Immediately' is the sense of paying cash down, on the spot; 'about' means the first pair of pieces wraps round the article and suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for fluctuating fortunes or moods, alternating highs and lows, used for changeable conditions.

clue.text: Estimates from the right assuming record increase

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the reversed word takes the record inside it
read from the right, the word for estimates runs backwards

parts.note: to put a value at a figure is to estimate it
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A valuer's figures, read backwards with a record included, show a rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' looks like supposing, but here it means taking on board, as the reversed estimate does with the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or rise in level or rate, a noun synonym for an increase.

clue.text: Become affected by ignoring party leaflet

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the party's letters are dropped

parts.note: to contract an illness is to become affected by it
Con is short for the Conservative party

explanation.surface: Someone is swayed by a leaflet without supporting any party.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTRACT loses CON, the Conservatives, under 'ignoring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pamphlet, especially a religious or political one, is a synonym for a leaflet.

clue.text: Language barrier initially faced by Poins after joke by Japanese-American

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word barrier

parts.note: the setter Poins refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A language barrier confronts the setter after a joke made by a Japanese-American.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for 'I', a common crossword device for 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Punjab region spanning India and Pakistan, an example of a language.

clue.text: Remarkable things of prophetic significance seen by female in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in places the female and the portent inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of prophetic significance

explanation.surface: Strange portents are witnessed by a woman in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary occurrences or marvels are plural examples of wonders, the plural of a striking event.

clue.text: Cross about mother taking time to find shoe cleaner

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for cross is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
ma is mother

explanation.surface: An angry mother takes her time looking for shoe polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like anger, but it is ROOD, the crucifix, which 'about' turns into DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat at the entrance on which people wipe their feet, so it cleans shoes; a whimsical description.

clue.text: Fellow reportedly carrying girl's basket

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the girl's name goes inside
reportedly says the word for fellow is heard, not written

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man is said to be holding a girl's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' applies to the fellow alone: the sound-alike jetty word is then wrapped round the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag or basket carried on a bicycle or a pack animal, one kind of basket.

clue.text: Soldiers calling for forgiveness of sins

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: Troops answer their vocation by seeking absolution.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology the pardoning of sins is called their remittance, a formal synonym for forgiveness.

clue.text: Somewhat inferior support prior to defeat

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to best someone is to defeat them

explanation.surface: Backing given before a loss looks rather poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Not quite top quality, the runner-up option, which is a fair synonym for slightly inferior.

clue.text: Similar to gripping second book

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the comparison word surrounds the moment

parts.note: as means like or similar to
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: Something resembles an exciting sequel novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' looks like praise for a page-turner, but it means holding, a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament, an example of a biblical book.

clue.text: Argument against joining clique

parts.note: a set is a group or clique
to can mean against, as in face pressed to the glass

explanation.surface: Someone opposes joining an exclusive group.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or heated quarrel, a brief scrap, an informal synonym for an argument.

clue.text: Property manager?

parts.note: looks like an estate agent or landlord, but the property is a theatre prop, the items a backstage worker handles

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre worker who moves scenery and props, which are stage properties, so a manager of them.

clue.text: Inappropriate for ailing duke to receive spell in prison

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the jail term goes inside

parts.note: ill means ailing
doing time is serving a prison spell

explanation.surface: A sick aristocrat is sentenced to jail at a bad moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming at the wrong moment makes something unsuitable, a synonym for unseasonable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Evidence of canoodling making Olive's bet look silly

indicators.note: a silly-looking version of the words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Olive's wager makes her look foolish when her neck gives away her kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left on the skin by amorous nibbling are proof that someone has been necking.

clue.text: Calls around noon after Washington's intimations of danger

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: around means the word for calls surrounds the letter for noon

parts.note: rings are telephone calls

explanation.surface: Washington receives midday phone calls warning of threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals or alerts that something bad may happen, plural synonyms for intimations of danger.

clue.text: Head ultimately shunned by every exotic dancer

indicators.note: exotic means strange and outlandish, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word for head is avoided

parts.note: nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is rejected by everyone at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately shunned' cuts NUT to NU, and 'exotic' mixes NU with EVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf, the Soviet-born ballet star who defected in 1961, is an example of a dancer.

clue.text: Treat irreverently disregarding note from girl

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so the note is dropped

parts.note: to violate a sacred place is to treat it irreverently
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone mistreats a girl while ignoring a message she left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is the sol-fa TE, which 'disregarding' removes from VIOLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Revealed by soldiers after party in the open air

indicators.note: after means the soldiers come behind the party

parts.note: something out is revealed or disclosed
a do is a party
OR, other ranks, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are exposed after a party held outside.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', soldiers below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Done or situated outside rather than under a roof, an adjective meaning in the fresh air.

clue.text: Expensive for an animal by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the animal's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: Something costly for an animal, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly or high-priced, a common British synonym for expensive.

clue.text: Going beyond the usual limits to get extra bit on suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect gets an additional bit to go beyond normal boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive, beyond reasonable bounds, especially of prices; literally out of the track or orbit.

clue.text: Blunder contributing to emperor retreating northward

indicators.note: northward says the hidden letters are read backwards
contributing to says the letters are part of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mistake helps an emperor's army fall back to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Blunder contributing' as the definition, but 'contributing to' signals the hidden letters, so the definition is just 'Blunder'. In a down clue 'northward' means read upwards, giving the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a mistake, so the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Quick to find unconventional fellow with note for Henry

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in the place of another

parts.note: a hippy is an unconventional, counter-culture type
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone quickly finds an oddball who swaps notes with Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a name, but it is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and fast-moving, informal British synonym for quick.

clue.text: Some introduced to embellish part of military uniform

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the word for some goes into the word for embellish

parts.note: to lard a speech is to embellish it
any means some, as in any bread

explanation.surface: Decorations added to a soldier's dress uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A braided cord worn round the shoulder, sometimes holding a whistle, is one component of uniform.

clue.text: Quarrelsome left back blocking a couple of Spurs' youngsters at the start

indicators.note: blocking means stuck between, so the reversed side goes between the two letters
a couple of means the first two letters of Spurs are taken
back says the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: at the start means the opening letter of youngsters

explanation.surface: A left-back stops two Tottenham Hotspur youth players early in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' looks like a football position, but it is the nautical word for left reversed. Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-tempered and argumentative, a British informal synonym for quarrelsome.

clue.text: Amuse with gossip implicating girl needing no introduction

indicators.note: implicating means involving, so the gossip word wraps round the cut name

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

indicators.note: the girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone entertains with scandal about a famous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' looks like praise for a celebrity, but it means the girl loses her first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain or distract, an older sense of the verb meaning to amuse.

clue.text: Wrong to have street artists seized in the outskirts of Albany

indicators.note: seized in means held inside, so the street and artists go inside
the outskirts are the outer letters of the word Albany

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Academy, or Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Street artists are arrested on the edge of Albany.
explanation.definitionFit: Off course or amiss, as in plans going awry, so an adverb meaning wrong.
